clue.text: Concern shown by substantial paper with hand-out for executive

parts.note: a concern is a firm or enterprise, a business
card is thick, stiff paper

explanation.surface: A company's affairs are reported in a weighty newspaper, with something handed out to its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as worry but is a firm; 'substantial paper' suggests a broadsheet but means thick paper stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Executives hand out small printed cards bearing their name and contact details when meeting people.

clue.text: Divorced out-of-work actor would welcome this

definitions.meaning: a resting actor longs to be offered a role in a play

explanation.surface: A divorced, unemployed actor would be glad of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word in two: an actor without work wants a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorced couples live separately; an idle performer wants a role, which splits the word into two.

clue.text: Instrument — use right one for stuffing snake

indicators.note: the right-and-one letters are used as the filling packed inside the snake

parts.note: a mamba is a venomous African snake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An odd cooking tip: use the correct item to stuff a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a large xylophone-like percussion instrument with wooden bars.

clue.text: Creature we found following end of line

indicators.note: following puts the word we after the letter taken from line
end of picks out the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: We discovered an animal trailing behind at the end of a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a farm animal, so it is a living creature.

clue.text: Excitedly gets eager for gift of chocolate

indicators.note: excitedly says the letters of gets eager are jumbled about in a lively way

explanation.surface: A child grows thrilled and keen at the prospect of a chocolate present.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow chocolate egg is the traditional present given at the spring festival marking the Resurrection.

clue.text: Musical instrument used by Ethiopian Orthodox

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical instrument played in the Ethiopian Orthodox church.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with hammers striking strings is a standard musical instrument.

clue.text: Part for barrels and large tubs returned by European

indicators.note: returned means the word for the large tubs is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: vats are large tubs or tanks for liquid

explanation.surface: A European cooper sends back components for barrels and big tubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrels are built from curved wooden strips called staves bound with hoops.

clue.text: So the referee finds a round concerning

parts.note: O is round in shape
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: As a result, the referee discovers something about a boxing round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' seems a mere opener but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean consequently or for that reason, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Hard water that is containing calcium, primarily

indicators.note: containing means the abbreviation for that is holds the next letter within it

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of calcium

explanation.surface: Hard water is the kind that holds chiefly calcium.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the chemistry of hard (limescale-forming) water; here 'hard water' is literally frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is solid, so it is water made hard.

clue.text: Visit Flint moving around in charge

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap about the abbreviation for in charge
moving says the letters of Flint are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in charge travels round the Welsh town of Flint on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' gives INFLT, which 'around' wraps about the abbreviation. Flint is a town in north Wales; 'Visit' means impose, not call on.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit a punishment or misfortune on someone is to impose it on them.

clue.text: Step across line for a position in the top three

definitions.text: a position in the top three

indicators.note: across says the step word stretches over the letter for line, which sits inside it

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A runner steps over the finish line to secure a podium spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse-race betting, a horse 'placed' finishes second or third (sometimes fourth), behind the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, finishing in a podium spot behind the winner earns this, as in bets each-way.

clue.text: Latent suspicion present following French and German articles

indicators.note: following says the word for present comes after the two articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a
der is a German definite article, the
current means present, of now

explanation.surface: A hidden doubt hangs about some French and German news articles.
explanation.definitionFit: An underlying feeling or tendency that runs beneath the surface, often of unease.

clue.text: Bishop wants libertine to slow down

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man

explanation.surface: A bishop wants a dissolute man to calm his pace of living.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply the brakes is to reduce speed, so the verb means decelerate.

clue.text: Partner past their best gets position on board

parts.note: stale means no longer fresh
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A spouse past their prime still lands a seat on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a boardroom but is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a stalemate is a position where the side to move has no legal move and is not in check.

clue.text: When to stop drinking in pub? None too soon

definitions.text: When to stop drinking in pub
definitions.meaning: drinking must end only at closing hour, which pubs call time
at last, after a wait that felt long

explanation.surface: Asking when drinkers should leave the pub, the answer is: not a moment early.
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs call 'time' at closing, the legal end of drinking hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when something long awaited finally happens, and literally names closing hour.

clue.text: Greek island with a type of fried pastry

parts.note: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: A Greek island known for a particular kind of fried pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a triangular South Asian pastry filled with spiced vegetables or meat and deep-fried.

clue.text: Roughly scrape pewter with energy to make cleaner

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are handled carelessly and come out in a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Scraping pewter hard and vigorously will make it clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet sweeper is a manual device with rotating brushes for cleaning floors, a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Rugby Union is supported by Twickenham's ultimate spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letter sits beneath, so it comes after the pair
ultimate picks out the last letter of Twickenham

explanation.surface: Rugby Union is backed by the final spirit of Twickenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home stadium of English rugby union, in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a distilled alcoholic drink, and spirits are such distilled liquors.

clue.text: Tons try to catch fish in seaweed

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Lots of people try fishing among the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for certain large brown seaweeds, kelp of the genus Laminaria.

clue.text: Finish off a date and rice mixture

indicators.note: mixture says the letters of a date and rice are blended together

explanation.surface: Polish off a mixed dish of dates and rice.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something completely, wiping it out, is to finish it off.

clue.text: Very unpleasant filth at university is on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: dirt is filth
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Dirtiness at the university is getting worse and nastier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotten and foul smelling is extremely disagreeable or nasty.

clue.text: Language of policeman leading to a habitual response

indicators.note: leading to says the word for policeman comes first, before the next piece

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A policeman's jargon becomes a reflex response.
explanation.definitionFit: Coptic is the liturgical tongue of the Egyptian Christian church, descended from ancient Egyptian.

clue.text: Being upstanding before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone must be of good character before a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' suggests honest, but here it is literal: standing upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean standing straight up, vertical rather than bent or lying.

clue.text: Pay for endless amusement

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off the word for pay for

parts.note: to fund something is to pay for it

explanation.surface: Spending money on never-ending entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment and amusement are synonyms for light-hearted pleasure.
